definitions.gloss: to wear out (clothing), to wear until shabby
definitions.explanation: To wear a piece of clothing so much over time that it becomes old, faded, or worn out. A compound of {着|き}る (to wear) and {古|ふる}す (to make old through use).

examples.japanese: {着古|きふる}したシャツを{捨|す}てた。
examples.english: I threw away a worn-out shirt.

examples.japanese: {着古|きふる}したジーンズが{一番|いちばん}{楽|らく}だ。
examples.english: Worn-in jeans are the most comfortable.

examples.japanese: セーターを{着古|きふる}して{毛玉|けだま}だらけになったが、{愛着|あいちゃく}があって{手放|てばな}せない。
examples.english: The sweater is worn out and covered in pilling, but I'm too attached to it to let it go.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly used in the past participle form {着古|きふる}した as an adjective modifying clothing. Can have either a negative connotation (shabby, ready to throw out) or a positive one (well-loved, comfortable through years of use).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {着古|きふる}したシャツ: a worn-out shirt
- {着古|きふる}したコート: a well-worn coat
- {着古|きふる}した{服|ふく}: worn-out clothes
- {着古|きふる}してよれよれ: worn out and limp
